obs: Sloan Shipyards Corp. v. United States Shipping Bd. Emergency Fleet Corporation

“The Shipping Act contemplated a corporation in which private persons might be stockholders and which was to be formed like any business corporation under the laws of the District, with capacity to sue and be sued.”

"the liability of national banks to suit 'as fully as natural persons' extends by implication to attachment and execution"; and "were intended to be subject to the incidents of suit, including attachment and execution"
Reconstruction Finance Corporation v. JG Menihan Corp.
"Starting from the premise indicated in the Keifer case that waivers by Congress of governmental immunity from suit should be liberally construed in the case of federal instrumentalities"
Franchise Tax Board v. United States Postal Service
"[W]e start from the premise that such waivers by Congress of governmental immunity in case of such federal instrumentalities should be liberally construed."
"[S]uch waivers by Congress of governmental immunity . . . should be liberally construed."
MacKey v. Lanier Collection Agency & Service, Inc.

“When Congress provides by law that an entity may sue and be sued, this includes all civil processes] incident to . . . legal proceedings including [gjarnishment and attachment. FHA v. Burr, 309 U. S. 242, 245-246 (1940). We have reaffirmed the view that a sue and be sued clause creates a presumption of susceptibility to garnishment and attachment in our more recent cases, as well.”
International Primate Protection League v. Administrators of Tulane Educational Fund
"(agencies authorized to \"sue and be sued\" are presumed to have fully waived immunity unless, as to particular types of suits, there is clearly a contrary legislative intent)."
United States v. Nordic Village, Inc.
"When authority is given, it is liberally construed."
"Absent such a showing, agencies \"authorized to `sue and be sued' are presumed to have fully waived immunity.\"
United States Postal Service v. Flamingo Industries (USA) Ltd.

“This Court has held that when Congress passes enabling legislation allowing an agency or other entity of the Federal Government to be sued the waiver should be given a liberal that is to say, expansive construction.”

“In establishing this mixed entity, Congress decided … that the TVA could ‘sue and be sued in its corporate name.’ … Without such a clause, the TVA … would have enjoyed sovereign immunity from suit… By instead providing that the TVA could ‘be sued,’ Congress waived at least some of the corporation’s immunity.”
